novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new measurement-oriented hypothesis that scientific foundation models encode cause and effect asymmetrically: “steering the cause direction should shift the model's prediction of the effect more than steering the effect direction shifts its prediction of the cause,” with the roles occupying “geometrically distinguishable subspaces.” Searches represented by terms such as “causal direction internal representations foundation models,” “cause effect asymmetry activation steering,” and “causal representation probing scientific models” found adjacent work—especially Geiger et al.’s causal-abstraction/interchange-intervention framework and Steinmann et al.’s 2024 “Learning Interpretable Concepts: Unifying Causal Representation Learning and Foundation Models”—but not the proposed bidirectional cause-versus-effect audit of pretrained scientific models. The step is a substantive multi-part adaptation of established probing, activation intervention, and causal-representation principles rather than a new intervention paradigm: defining and combining directional interventional and predictive asymmetry across known scientific mechanisms merits standard novelty, but the core intuition follows naturally from existing causal representation learning.
